title: "Structured covariance for group-specific effects"

## Latent effects, not correlated residuals

For a Bernoulli model, the linear predictor can contain several latent trajectories:

$$
\operatorname{logit}(p_i) = x_i^T\beta + \sum_b u_{b,g_b(i),t_i},
\qquad u_{b,g} \sim N(0, D_b R_b D_b).
$$

Groups within each block are independent conditional on its covariance parameters.
Different blocks are also independent in the prior; their posterior effects need
not be independent. The response still follows the ordinary Bernoulli likelihood.
For Gaussian observations, the latent covariance adds to observation noise after
integrating out latent effects. It does not replace residual noise.

## Multiple trajectories

```python
import bambi as bmb

formula = (
    "outcome ~ x1 + x2"
    " + ar1(0 + year | subject)"
    " + ar1(0 + year | subject:condition)"
    " + ar1(0 + year | subject:context)"
    " + ar1(0 + year | subject:condition:context)"
)
model = bmb.Model(formula, data, family="bernoulli")
```

Use `proportion(successes, trials)` as the response and `family="binomial"`
for aggregated binomial observations. Aggregation is valid only when all trials
in a row share the same predictors and latent cells.

The first block is shared by observations from one subject. The final block is
shared only within one subject/condition/context combination. Replicate rows at
the same time share a latent coefficient, but response noise remains separate.
Use a crossed design with enough observations to distinguish variance components.
When grouping partitions coincide, component estimates can depend strongly on priors.

## Structures and priors

| Formula term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ar1(0 + year \| subject)` | Stationary AR1; correlation `rho ** abs(year_i - year_j)` |
| `ou(0 + time \| subject)` | Continuous-time correlation `exp(-decay * distance)` |
| `cs(0 + visit \| subject)` | One correlation between different visit levels |
| `toep(0 + year \| subject, max_lag=5)` | Finite positive-definite Toeplitz correlation |
| `us(0 + C(visit) \| subject)` | Unstructured covariance across visits |
| `us(1 + x \| subject)` | Correlated intercept and slope |

AR1 and Toeplitz require numeric integer times. Missing years retain their actual
gaps. OU accepts fractional times. Recenter or rescale extreme time magnitudes
above `2**52` before fitting.

**Scale limitation:** temporal/exchangeable blocks use one marginal SD per term,
shared across its groups and times. Unstructured blocks use one SD per coefficient.
Heterogeneous temporal scales and scale regression are deferred.

```python
term = "ar1(0 + year | subject)"
model = bmb.Model(
    f"outcome ~ x1 + {term}", data, family="bernoulli",
    priors={term: {
        "sd": bmb.Prior("HalfNormal", sigma=0.7),
        "rho": bmb.Prior("Normal", mu=0, sigma=0.5),
    }},
)
```

Correlation priors are truncated to valid support. Defaults regularize correlations
and partial autocorrelations with Normal(0, 0.5), use Exponential(1) for OU decay,
and LKJ(2) for unstructured correlation. Default latent SD priors are HalfNormal
with scale 2.5 on non-Gaussian link scales; Gaussian parent effects use 2.5 times
the response SD. Set explicit priors for substantive analysis and reference matching.

Unstructured keys are `sd` and `eta`; a fixed `correlation` matrix can replace
`eta`. Toeplitz uses `partial`, one partial autocorrelation per lag, not a vector
of ordinary autocorrelations. Fixed numeric hyperparameters are accepted too.

## Prediction

```python
model.predict(idata, data=target_data, kind="response_params")
model.predict(idata, data=target_data, kind="response")
model.predict(idata, data=target_data, include_group_specific=False)
```

Existing cells keep their posterior effects. AR1/OU interpolation and extrapolation
draw all requested times jointly, conditional on fitted coefficients. New subjects
receive population trajectories. A new three-way combination can retain known
subject and two-way effects while receiving a new three-way trajectory.

CS and unstructured visit effects require declared levels. Toeplitz requires the
combined fitted/target time span to remain within `max_lag`. New latent cells do not
have fitted pointwise conditional log likelihoods; use a suitable held-out refit
for model assessment. Repeated calls do not persist newly sampled latent cells.

## Validation and resource use

The implementation is under validation. Small construction and prediction checks
are not evidence of posterior agreement with brms or Stan. The reference scripts
and outstanding gates are described in
[the validation guide](../examples/group_covariance_validation/README.md).

Use prior predictive checks before fitting, then convergence diagnostics, posterior
predictive checks, calibration and prior sensitivity. A four-block binary model
can need substantially more data than a simple random-intercept model.

On a constrained laptop, run only small serial checks with one numerical thread.
Run reference fits, the full backend matrix, and simulation calibration on suitable
hardware. This page never executes fitting during rendering.
